brief_answer: Enforcement is very unlikely (reference range 5–15%). §925: Zhao primarily resided and worked in CA and was not individually represented → the Texas forum and choice-of-law clauses are voidable at his election (he has already invoked it) → CA law and CA forum. Under §16600/§16600.5 the covenant is void regardless of where signed; SB 699 makes an enforcement attempt itself a civil violation with fee-shifting. Even under Restatement §187 analysis (DeSantis/Nedlloyd/Application Group), CA has the materially greater interest and a fundamental policy. Texas law would require reasonableness (24 months nationwide likely over-broad → reformation, §15.51(c)), but Texas law will not be applied. Client exposure: §16600.5(e) fees/damages for attempting enforcement; §16600.1 notice never sent → UCL exposure. Recommendation: do not sue; protect trade secrets via §10 and DTSA/CUTSA if evidence arises; consider non-solicit (§9) analysis separately.
